# Pattern Editor

## Purpose

The Pattern Editor is the user-side tool used to create the textile pattern before running the machine. The user draws a three-colour image and exports it as a `.png` file, which is then transferred to the Raspberry Pi through a USB flash drive.

## Workflow

```text
Open the Pattern Editor
        ↓
Draw the desired three-colour pattern
        ↓
Export the image as a PNG file
        ↓
Copy the PNG file to the USB flash drive
        ↓
Select the file from the machine display
```

## Pattern Constraints

The current control software accepts patterns with the following properties:

| Parameter | Requirement |
|---|---|
| File format | `.png` |
| Image width | Exactly 48 pixels |
| Number of colours | Exactly 3 distinct RGB colours |
| USB storage location | Files stored directly in the root folder of the USB drive |

The image height is not fixed: it determines the length of the produced pattern.

## Automatic Colour Association

When a pattern is started, the Raspberry Pi reads the image pixels in sequence and associates the three colours to the three servo-controlled yarn channels in order of first occurrence:

| Colour order in the PNG | Command sent to ESP32 | Yarn actuator |
|---|---|---|
| First distinct colour found | `C1` | Servo 1 |
| Second distinct colour found | `C2` | Servo 2 |
| Third distinct colour found | `C3` | Servo 3 |

Before starting production, the user must place the real yarns according to the colour-to-servo mapping shown in the Raspberry Pi terminal.

## Transfer to the Machine

Store the exported PNG files directly on the USB flash drive:

```text
USB_DRIVE/
├── pattern_01.png
├── pattern_02.png
└── pattern_03.png
```

The machine interface will list these files on the GFX HAT display.
